claims.text: Feb 2007 (signed in Washington, reported 9 Feb 2007) DHS Secretary Michael Chertoff and Israeli Public Security Minister Avi Dichter signed a homeland-security MOU: counterterrorism and serious crime, aviation (passenger and cargo) security, training and exchange of analytical personnel, explosives-detection R&D, emergency-planning information; communication via embassy channels; 'does not independently authorize disclosure of classified information'; 'does not impose any legal commitments'; third-party sharing requires originator consent.

22 USC 8606(c), enacted by the US-Israel Strategic Partnership Act 2014 (P.L. 113-296 §7, 19 Dec 2014), authorized DHS through HSARPA with State concurrence to set up pilot cooperative research programs with Israel on border, maritime and aviation security, explosives detection and emergency services; P.L. 114-304 (2016) dropped 'pilot' and added cybersecurity; P.L. 116-283 authorized $2m for FY2021.

FY2022 NDAA (P.L. 117-81 §1551, 27 Dec 2021) created a DHS US–Israel cybersecurity grant program for joint ventures, at least 50% non-federal cost share, unclassified projects only, advisory board incl BSF and BIRD nominees, DNI counterintelligence screen; authorized not less than $6m a year FY2022–2026. Introduced Apr 2021 by Collins, Rosen, Whitehouse, Young; House amendment by Garbarino passed 23 Sep 2021.

BIRD HLS: since 2016 DHS S&T and Israel's Ministry of Public Security have partnered with the BIRD Foundation to fund US–Israeli company pairs; conditional grants up to $1m; 2020 round $1.5m to two projects (about $3m with private money). MOPS chief scientist Gad Frishman: it 'enables us to enhance public safety in Israel and in the United States.'

ow6_police.topic: Police exchanges, critics, NYPD Israel office, ICE tools

claims.text: GILEE founded 1992 at Georgia State University by criminologist Robert Friedmann ahead of 1996 Atlanta Olympics; GILEE site: over 1,100 officials, 290 programs (Reason 2022); about 1,250 executives in exchanges by 2023 and ~43,000 at workshops/conferences (Atlanta Jewish Times via Wikipedia). Bernard Marcus foundation gave at least $1.25m since 2005; Atlanta PD at least $25,500/yr 2017–21, says no federal money for Israel training.

JINSA began bringing US police to Israel summer 2002 (program created by former FBI assistant director Steven Pomerantz), pays participants' costs; Marcus foundation gave JINSA at least $2.38m since 2011. ADL Advanced Training School 2002, Israel seminars from 2004; ~$115,000 per trip plus ~$200,000/yr staff; departments ~$5,000 per officer. DHS grants paid $480,466 for police trips abroad since 2015, over 80% for Israel training.

DOJ COPS Office (2013) described JINSA LEEP, established after 9/11, as teaching intelligence gathering and sharing, early plot detection, post-incident forensics and terrorist ideologies: 'if properly trained, U.S. law enforcement can better prevent and respond to terrorist threats.'

JTA (2022): more than 1,000 people, mostly senior law enforcement, have taken ADL, JINSA and GILEE trips; ADL paused trips in 2019; a June 2020 draft memo by George Selim and Greg Ehrie recommended ending them but warned ending 'could imply culpability when ADL does not believe we did anything wrong'; ADL decided to continue with a revised curriculum. Reason: program suspended, not resumed; ADL says it does no practical field training.

Amnesty USA (25 Aug 2016) said since 2002 ADL, AJC Project Interchange and JINSA paid for police chiefs to train in Israel; named Baltimore after the DOJ's 10 Aug 2016 Baltimore report; argued trainees are exposed to systems with documented abuses; 'Israel is not such a partner.'

JVP launched Deadly Exchange in 2017, report 2018: 'these programs facilitate an exchange of methods in state violence and control.' Reason: less evidence training causes US excessive force; claims US officers learn chokeholds in Israel have no evidence; Israel Police, JINSA, ADL deny. Friedmann says Israeli use-of-force rules 'much more restrictive'.

Durham NC city council on 16 Apr 2018 unanimously adopted: 'The council opposes international exchanges with any country in which Durham officers receive military-style training'; Chief CJ Davis said Durham had not initiated or joined any Israel exchange under her.

Dec 2018: Vermont State Police and Northampton MA police chief withdrew from the ADL New England seminar in Israel (2–11 Dec 2018) after resident pressure; ADL New England has run it annually since 2002.
NYPD opened a branch at Israel Police headquarters in Kfar Saba (reported 7 Sep 2012), staffed by detective Charlie Ben-Naim, rather than at the US embassy.

City & State (21 Aug 2026): NYPD stationed an officer in Israel from 2007 under its liaison program; office at Sharon District HQ in Kfar Saba since 2012; Det. Charlie Benaim one of more than a dozen liaison officers; program partly funded by NYC Police Foundation (trustees include Andrew and Alexander Tisch); NYPD contracts Terrogence Global; trips as recently as Sept 2025; Mamdani has not directed the NYPD to stop cooperating; NYPD says no trips planned this year.

ICE signed $2m contract with Israeli-founded Paragon Solutions (Graphite spyware) in late 2024; paused for review under EO 14093 (Wired, 21 Oct 2024); Guardian 2 Sep 2025 reported procurement records show the pause lifted with ICE as contracting agency; Paragon now owned by a US firm (AE Industrial/RED Lattice).

ICE bought Cellebrite phone-extraction technology for $2.2m in March 2017 and on 24 Jun 2019 gave notice of intent to award up to $30–35m for Universal Forensic Extraction Devices, licences, training.
